nodes.name: Peat moss
nodes.desc: Bog moss that builds the wet peat of raised bogs such as Kuresoo, the best-known bog in the park.

nodes.name: Floodplain sedges & grasses
nodes.desc: Sedges of the riverside meadows that spend each spring under floodwater and feed many grazers.

nodes.name: Scots pine
nodes.desc: Conifer of the drier forest and bog edges, whose twigs and bark browsers use in winter.

nodes.name: Willows
nodes.desc: Waterside trees and shrubs; willow is a staple food and building material for beavers.

nodes.name: Field vole
nodes.desc: Small grass-eating rodent of damp meadows and a staple prey for foxes, buzzards and cranes.

nodes.name: European hare
nodes.desc: Grazer of open ground that lynx turn to when roe deer are scarce.

nodes.name: Mallard
nodes.desc: Dabbling duck of flooded meadows and rivers that eats plant matter and small invertebrates.

nodes.name: Eurasian beaver
nodes.desc: Eats waterside plants and the bark and shoots of willow, aspen and birch. Its dams create wetland habitat for otters and others.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: One of the most numerous large mammals in the park. An omnivore that roots for plants and small animals.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: A numerous browser of shoots and herbs, and the preferred prey of lynx in Estonia.

nodes.name: Elk (moose)
nodes.desc: Large browser of willow and pine twigs, and one of the park's most numerous big mammals.

nodes.name: Common crane
nodes.desc: Breeds and gathers on the bogs and floodplain; about a thousand gather here in autumn. Eats plants, voles and other small animals.

nodes.name: Eurasian otter
nodes.desc: Hunts along rivers and beaver wetlands. Recorded eating ducks, frogs and snakes.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: Raptor of forest edges and meadows that hunts voles, hares and other small animals.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Generalist hunter of voles, hares and ducks that also scavenges carcasses.

nodes.name: Eurasian lynx
nodes.desc: Ambush hunter. In Estonia roe deer are its main prey, with hares, beavers and foxes taken too.

nodes.name: Grey wolf
nodes.desc: Pack hunter of moose, roe deer and wild boar, and a top predator of the forest.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: Omnivore that takes young deer and moose, beavers and carrion as well as plant foods.

nodes.name: Spring flood
nodes.desc: Snowmelt from the uplands spreads over meadows and forests each spring, flooding up to 175 square kilometres.

nodes.name: Snowmelt & winter
nodes.desc: Winter snow and ice that melt into the yearly flood and shape how easily deer and moose can feed.

nodes.name: Peat & bog
nodes.desc: Wet raised-bog peat and swamp-forest soils that anchor mosses and trees.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer light that drives growth of meadow plants and trees.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi and microbes that break down dead plants and carcasses into nutrients.
